from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [

            "Clockwise area is negative.",

            "This measures 2D reach clearance."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites & The 2D 'Shadow'", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup vectors and parallelogram

        self.place_at_grid(u, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(v, 'C3')
        
        # Helper to create parallelogram
        def get_para(v1, v2):
            return Polygon(ORIGIN, v1.get_end(), v1.get_end() + v2.get_end(), v2.get_end(), fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        para = get_para(u, v)
        self.play(FadeIn(u), FadeIn(v), Create(para))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeTransform(para.copy(), para.set_color(GRAY)))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        para_cw = get_para(v, u).set_fill(color="#FF0000")
        self.play(FadeOut(para), FadeIn(para_cw))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF0000")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        para_ccw = get_para(u, v).set_fill(color="#0000FF")
        self.play(FadeOut(para_cw), FadeIn(para_ccw))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#0000FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(para_ccw.animate.scale(1.2))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Algebraic Mechanic: Determinant Method", 
                          ["Use 3x3 determinant with unit vectors.", 
                           "Expand using minor 2x2 determinants.", 
                           "Calculate i, j, and k components."])
        
        # Matrix Setup
        matrix_str = r"""
        \begin{vmatrix}
        \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\
        a_x & a_y & a_z \\
        b_x & b_y & b_z
        \end{vmatrix}
        """
        matrix = MathTex(matrix_str, font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Write(matrix))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
                  self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Minor determinants
        minor1 = MathTex(r"\mathbf{i} \begin{vmatrix} a_y & a_z \\ b_y & b_z \end{vmatrix}", color=BLUE)
        minor2 = MathTex(r"-\mathbf{j} \begin{vmatrix} a_x & a_z \\ b_x & b_z \end{vmatrix}", color=GREEN)
        minor3 = MathTex(r"+\mathbf{k} \begin{vmatrix} a_x & a_y \\ b_x & b_y \end{vmatrix}", color=RED)
        
        minors = VGroup(minor1, minor2, minor3).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(minors, 'D4', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(minors))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
                  self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        result = MathTex(r"\vec{v} = (a_y b_z - a_z b_y)\mathbf{i} - (a_x b_z - a_z b_x)\mathbf{j} + (a_x b_y - a_y b_x)\mathbf{k}", font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(result, 'F3', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(result))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Mastering the Cross Product: From 2D intuition to 3D mechanics

sections.title: Prerequisites & The 2D 'Shadow' (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Briefly review vectors and dot products. Introduce the 2D Cross Product (Determinant) as a measure of the 'signed area' of a parallelogram formed by two vectors. Visual: A 2D plane where vectors u and v span a parallelogram; shaded area turns red if clockwise, blue if counter-clockwise.
sections.example: A robotic arm's 2D reach: calculate the area of the quadrilateral formed by two joints to ensure clearance.

sections.title: Transition to 3D: The Geometry of Space (0:45-2:00)
sections.content: Explain that in 3D, the cross product result is a vector, not a scalar. Key properties: 1. Orthogonality (result is perpendicular to the plane of the two vectors). 2. Magnitude = Area of parallelogram. 3. Direction follows the Right-Hand Rule.
sections.example: Visualizing a spinning propeller: The two blades form vectors, the cross product vector points along the axis of rotation.

sections.title: The Algebraic Mechanic: Determinant Method (2:00-3:30)
sections.content: Introduce the formal computation using the 3x3 determinant with unit vectors i, j, k. Break down the expansion by minors, emphasizing the pattern of cross-multiplication. Visual: Matrix setup animating into three separate 2x2 determinants.
sections.example: Calculating the i, j, and k components of the cross product for vectors A=(1,2,3) and B=(4,5,6) to find the normal vector of a surface.

sections.title: Physical Application: Torque (3:30-4:30)
sections.content: Apply the cross product to physics. Torque (τ) = r × F. Explain how the cross product captures both the force magnitude and the distance from the pivot point effectively.
sections.example: A squirrel pushing on a circular door handle: The cross product shows how the angle of the squirrel's push (force vector) relative to the handle (position vector) determines how fast the door swings.

sections.title: Summary & Quick Recall (4:30-5:00)
sections.content: Recap: 2D gives area (scalar), 3D gives a perpendicular vector. Emphasize: The Right-Hand Rule is the 'North Star' for direction.
sections.example: A quick interactive flash-test: Show two vectors in 3D space; ask the student to point their thumb in the direction of the cross product.
